 Prayer:

Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of the
 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the Judgment and decree dated
 22.04.2022 made in M.C.O.P.No.2541 of 2019 on the file of the Motor
 Accident Claims Tribunal, (Iii Court of Small Causes), Chennai.

For Appellant : Mr.R.Nalliyappan
 For R2 : M/s.C.Bhuvanasundari
 Judgment

The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the Award dated 22.04.2022 made in M.C.O.P.No.2541 of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2019 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (III Court of Small Causes), Chennai.

sentences.text: 2. The appeal is filed seeking enhancement of compensation.
The parties shall be referred to as per their ranking in the Tribunal.
2. The claim petition was filed by the widowed-mother of the deceased Dhayalan who died in a motor accident which occurred on 05.04.2019.
According to the claimant, her son aged about 24 years at the time of accident was working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

Vijaya vs M.Saravanan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128295539/
1 3.
The first respondent as the owner of the vehicle remained exparte before the Tribunal.
The second respondent contested the claim petition by filing a counter disputing negligence, quantum and liability.
5. Before the Claims Tribunal, the claimant examined herself as P.W.1 and one witness was examined as P.W.2 and documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 were marked.
On the side of the respondents, no witness was examined and no document was marked.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

The Claims Tribunal on a assessment of the entire evidence on record awarded a sum of Rs.19,85,200/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
7.
Not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of loss of dependency, the claimant has preferred the above appeal.

8. The learned counsel appearing for the claimant submitted that the deceased was aged about 24 years at the time of accident and was working as a driver which was evidenced by Ex.P.9 - Driving licence of the deceased.
The learned counsel further submitted that the accident took place in the year 2019 and therefore the assessment of income at Rs.12,000/- p.m. was very much on the lower side.
The learned counsel fairly submitted that the award under the conventional heads was fair and reasonable and therefore, the same could be confirmed.
9. The learned counsel for the second respondent on the other hand submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal was just, fair and reasonable and did not call for any interference in this appeal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10
. I have heard both the learned counsels and I have also perused the materials available on record .
11. The only point canvassed in the appeal is the assessment towards loss of dependency.
According to the claimant, the income assessed was erroneous under the facts and circumstances of case.
The accident indisputably occurred in 2019 and the deceased who was aged 24 years at that time was working as a driver.
Ex . P.9, the driving license of the deceased was filed in support of the deceased's avocation.

I am therefore of the view that the income needs to be re-fixed as per the decision of the Hon'ble Division of this Court in Andal and two others v. Avinav Kannan and another reported in 2019(1) TN MAC 54(DB).
12.

Following the judgment of the Honble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others Vs.Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 50% of the income is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased who died as a bachelor.

sentences.text: 40% of the income is added towards future prospects and the multiplier 18, appropriate to the age of the deceased is adopted.
The compensation awarded under the other heads are reasonable and therefore, they are not interfered.

14. In the light of the above discussions, the award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Heads and Calculation Compensation enhanced by this Court (Rs.) Loss of Dependency :

Monthly Income : Rs.14,108/-
 Add : Future Prospects @ 40% : Rs. 5,463/-
 -------------
 : Rs.19,751/-

Annual loss of Income (19,751 x12) : Rs.2,37,012/-
 * Multiplier applicable with  reference to the age : 26  (2,37,012 x18) : Rs.42,66,216/-
 21,3  Less : 50% deduction  (Rs.42,66,216/- - 50%) : Rs.21,33,108/-
 Loss of Estate
Funeral Expenses
Transport Expenses   Loss of Love and affection to the appellant

Medical bills   Total *23  * Rounded off to Rs.23,04,000/-
15.
Thus, the claimant would be entitled to a further sum of Rs.3,18,800/- together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

Vijaya vs M.Saravanan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128295539/
3 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 16.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claimant that the appeal was filed with a delay of 104 days and this Court at the time of condoning the delay ordered that the claimant shall not be entitled to interest for the delay period of 104 days.
It is therefore made clear that the claimant shall not be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation for the delay period of 104 days.
17. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent that the amount awarded by the Tribunal has already been deposited and withdrawn by the claimant.

18. In the result,
(i) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
ii) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.19,85,200/- to Rs.23,04,000/-.

The claimant shall be entitled to a further sum of Rs.3,18,800/- which shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till deposit, less the interest for the delay period of 104 days in filing appeal.

(iii)The second respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced amount along with interest as stated above, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(iii)On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the enhanced award amount along with accrued interest, after filing appropriate application before the Tribunal.
(iv)The claimant is directed to pay the Court Fee for the enhanced compensation, if any, and the Registry is directed to draft the decree only after the payment of Court fee.
No costs.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Following the said Division Bench Judgment and by applying the inflation index as per notification No.370142(E)(No.26/2008) (F.No.370/42/3/2008-TPL), dated 13.06.2006 issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, the income of the deceased is arrived at Rs.14,108/- per month.

14. In the light of the above discussions, the award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:-

 Loss of Estate
It is therefore made clear that the claimant shall not be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation for the delay period of 104 days.
18. In the result,
(i) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
ii) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.19,85,200/- to Rs.23,04,000/-.
The claimant shall be entitled to a further sum of Rs.3,18,800/- which shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till deposit, less the interest for the delay period of 104 days in filing appeal.
(iii)The second respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced amount along with interest as stated above, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(iii)On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the enhanced award amount along with accrued interest, after filing appropriate application before the Tribunal.
(iv)The claimant is directed to pay the Court Fee for the enhanced compensation, if any, and the Registry is directed to draft the decree only after the payment of Court fee.
No costs.
